title: Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d)
description: ⭐️ Your Impact: The European trades are one of the least digitised industries left. Software penetration sits under 15%, against roughly 70% in the US. The labour productivity gap runs about 30%. Millions of skilled people spend their evenings on paperwork instead of the craft they trained for — in the industry that has to deliver the energy transition. There is almost no incumbent software to displace. That is unusual, and it won't last. smalt replaces the back office entirely rather than selling Meister another tool to manage. In the last six months that went from a partner app and a dashboard to around thirty AI agents in production - pricing real jobs, qualifying real leads, running the operations of businesses whose payroll depends on it working. These days building thirty agents is easy. Knowing which thirty is what's challenging. That only comes from being in the Betrieb and talking to the Handwerker. That's what this role is for. What you'll do You'll sit in Handwerksbetrieben - at the Meister's desk, in the van, on site, next to our team - and watch how the work actually happens. Then you'll come back and build the thing that fixes it, often multiple times on the same day. - Spend real time with partners. Not a quarterly customer call. You'll know our Meister by name, understand their P&L, and notice the thing they've stopped complaining about because they assume it can't be fixed. - Build across the stack. Python/FastAPI services, Vue interfaces, Flutter screens, agent loops, data pipelines - whatever the problem needs. - Own agents in production. Not demos. Agents that price real jobs, answer real customers, and cost real money when they're wrong. Reliability, evaluation, structured output, graceful failure. - Decide what to build. You'll write your own acceptance criteria. Nobody here will hand you a spec, and waiting for one is how to fail in this role. - Measure whether it worked. Hours saved per partner, offers that go out untouched, leads answered before a competitor picks up. If the number didn't move, it didn't work. What that looks like in practice In July one of our Meister got an early build of the partner app, ahead of the general rollout. He tested it between jobs and sent screenshots: from a calendar appointment he could no longer jump into the project to pull the customer's phone number. He had a reply in two minutes. Within the hour he'd also asked for a navigation button - tap the address, go straight to maps. Neither was news. Both were already being worked on before he hit send. We aim to be fast, and close enough to the work that we've usually seen the problem before the person living it has to tell us. ✨ What Makes You a Great Fit: You might be a great fit if you - Have owned something end to end - architecture through delivery through the unglamorous iteration afterwards. We don't count years; we look at what you carried. - Get obsessed with a problem rather than a stack. The tools change every few months. The curiosity compounds. - Would rather ship something that changes a tradesperson's week than win an argument about abstractions. - Actually like talking to customers, and have changed your mind about a feature because of something a user said. - Are comfortable being the least knowledgeable person in a room full of electricians, and ask the question anyway. - Can hold "ship it today" and "this needs to survive two years" in your head at the same time, and know which one applies. Our stack, so you know what you're walking into: - Backend: Python, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL (with pgvector), Celery, Redis - Frontend: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, PrimeVue - Mobile: Flutter - AI: Anthropic, Open source and Google models, vector search over partner and catalog data - Infra: Google Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Sentry We care that you're strong somewhere and unafraid everywhere else. If you've never written Vue but you've shipped production systems and you learn fast, that is fine - several of us hadn't either. What we do look for: - Production experience with LLM-powered features, and the scars that come with it: evaluation, structured output parsing, context management, error recovery - A track record of shipping things people actually used - High agency. You'll get context and constraints, not instructions. - Raw intelligence paired with a humble mindset German is helpful and you'll pick some up either way - our partners speak it all day. It isn't a requirement but definitely a nice to have. The the team works in English. ☀️ Why You'll Love Working With Us: - Top-of-market compensation and a meaningful VSOP package - Direct access to real users and short feedback loops - Real ownership, and direct proximity to the founders - and to General Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures and Heartfelt - A team of five engineers who have shipped more in six months than most teams do in two years, and who set the pace themselves Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will contribute to the development and validation of our multi-UAV system, with a particular focus on software tooling, simulation, and system observability. 

Depending on your background and the project, you may also contribute to areas such as SLAM, navigation, perception, planning, or multi-agent coordination.   • Develop data-driven dashboards and tools to monitor, analyze, and visualize system performance
  • Extend our simulation framework with KPIs, automated scenarios, and evaluation workflows

  • Contribute to the core robotics stack in areas such as estimation, perception, planning, control, or mission execution
  • Collaborate closely with robotics, simulation, embedded, and domain experts

Your profile

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master's degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Autonomous Systems, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
  • Good programming skills in C++, ideally modern C++ (17/20)
  • Solid foundation in algorithms, data structures, and software engineering
  • Basic understanding of robotics concepts such as coordinate frames, sensor data, estimation, planning, or control
  • Comfortable working in Linux

  • Experience working with LiDAR or camera data
  • Exposure to PX4 or ArduPilot
  • Experience with simulation frameworks such as Gazebo, Isaac Sim, or Unreal Engine
  • Experience with embedded platforms, GPUs, or networking
  • Exposure to machine learning methods


What else

raw.title: Data Architecture Consultant (m/w/d)
raw.description:
Welcome

Du möchtest komplexe Datenlandschaften gestalten und Unternehmen beim Aufbau zukunftsfähiger Datenarchitekturen unterstützen? Dann bist du bei INVENSITY genau richtig. Als internationale Technologie- und Innovationsberatung begleiten wir unsere Kunden bei anspruchsvollen Digitalisierungs-, Transformations- und Migrationsprojekten.

Dein Beitrag: Als Data Architecture Consultant entwickelst du Ziel-Datenarchitekturen und Datenmodelle, optimierst Datenflüsse und unterstützt unsere Kunden dabei, deren Datenqualität zu etablieren.


Was erwartet dich?

  • Entwickle Ziel-Datenarchitekturen und übergreifende Datenmodelle für komplexe Unternehmensumgebungen unserer Kunden 
  • Analysiere und optimiere Datenflüsse, Schnittstellen und Systemintegrationen
  • Entwickle Konzepte für Data Governance, Datenqualität und einheitliche Datenstandards 
  • Berate unsere Kunden bei der Auswahl und Integration neuer Datenbanken, Datenplattformen und Cloud-Lösungen
  • Unterstütze Digitalisierungs- und Migrationsprojekte und stimme Anforderungen mit Fachbereichen, IT und weiteren Stakeholdern ab
  • Berücksichtige Datenschutz-, Datensicherheits- und Compliance-Anforderungen bei der Gestaltung von Datenarchitekturen
  • Wissensaustasch und Mentoring: Teile dein Fachwissen in Workshops, Coachings und Projekten und lerne gleichzeitig von anderen Experten
  • Persönliche und fachliche Weiterentwicklung: Wachse in einem technologisch führenden Umfeld, knüpfe Kontakte und gestalte Innovationen in den unterschiedlichsten Branchen


Was bringst du mit?

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Data Science oder eines vergleichbaren Studiengangs 
  • Mindestens drei Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Entwicklung oder Optimierung von Datenarchitekturen
  • Fundierte Kenntnisse in Datenmodellierung, Datenintegration oder Datenmanagement (z.B. Data Warehousing) 
  • Kenntnisse in Cloud-Technologien wie Microsoft Azure, AWS oder Google Cloud sind von Vorteil 
  • Erfahrung mit Data Governance, Datenqualitätsstandards sowie Datenschutz- und Compliance-Anforderungen
  • Eine analytische und strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Kommunikationsstärke und Erfahrung in agilen Projektumgebungen
  • Reisebereitschaft für nationale Projekteinsätze bei unseren Kunden vor Ort 
  • Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und fließende Englischkenntnisse


Was sind deine Vorteile?

  • Strukturiertes Onboarding: Ein klarer Startplan, gemeinsame Starttage mit anderen Neustartern und feste Ansprechpartner unterstützen dich beim Einstieg
  • Flexibles Arbeiten: Unbefristete Arbeitsverträge, flexible Arbeitszeiten, Home-Office-Option, Teilzeit und Sabbatical-Möglichkeiten
  • Globales Netzwerk: Zusammenarbeit mit Experten an unseren internationalen Standorten
  • Einzigartige Atmosphäre und wertschätzende Unternehmenskultur: Durch monatliche Office Events, Du-Kultur, schnelle Kommunikationswege und die Arbeit an gemeinsamen Zielen
  • Steile Lernkurve: Durch abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben in einem innovativen Umfeld mit vielfältigen Projekten in verschiedenen Branchen und mit verschiedenen Kunden
  • Persönliche und fachliche Weiterentwicklung: Individuelles Mentoring und Coaching, ACADEMY-Trainings und Feedback-Kultur
  • Attraktive Aufstiegschancen: Transparente Karrierewege inklusive schneller Übernahme verantwortungsvoller Aufgaben und internationaler Karrieremöglichkeiten
  • Leistungsbezogenes Vergütungspaket: Feste und variable Gehaltsbestandteile sowie halbjährliche Assessments
  • Mobilitätszuschuss: Möglichkeit der Übernahme einer BahnCard 50 


Good to know

Arbeitsort: Hybrid (Homeoffice und Büro)

You will be treated as a full member of the team, expected to take a research question from literature to a working prototype and to present your results to the people who make the investment decisions. You bring depth, or the ambition to build it, in at least one relevant toolkit, whether that is graph ML and graph databases (e.g. PyTorch Geometric), LLM tooling, tool use and evaluation, or probabilistic modeling (e.g. PyMC, NumPyro). With Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) we would work on a graph-structured database, where people and companies are nodes and the relationships between them are part of the data, and ask what that structure can tell us that a table cannot. 2. With Program-aided Language Models (PAL) we would have the model write a small program for every number it pulls from decks and financial statements, so figures are accurately computed, because that is what makes it safe to point a language model at financial data. 3. And with Bayesian Updating we would keep our recorded understanding of a company moving as new evidence arrives, since the investment process is iterative and a view written down two years ago should not still be the view today. Real Data: Proprietary venture data that researchers rarely get access to, with the pipelines to use it productively. Interested? Deine Arbeitsweise ist value-driven, du priorisierst konsequent nach dem, was für Nutzer:innen und Geschäft wirklich zählt
  • Du verantwortest verlässliche Lieferung, Systemstabilität und Verfügbarkeit deines Verantwortungsbereichs und sorgst für den gezielten Abbau technischer Schulden.
  • Die gezielte Weiterbildung jedes einzelnen Teammitglieds ist dir enorm wichtig, bei uns ist das kein Nice-to-have, sondern fester Bestandteil unserer Ziele.
  • Du entwickelst dein Team aktiv und zukunftsorientiert weiter, technisch wie organisatorisch, und machst es so fit für ein sich schnell änderndes Umfeld.
  • Du führst dein Team gemeinsam mit der Produktmanagerin als Doppelspitze.
  • Du arbeitest eng mit den anderen Engineering Managern, dem Senior Software Architekten und dem Head of Development zusammen.
  • Du treibst Recruiting und Onboarding neuer Teammitglieder aktiv mit voran.

  • Freude daran, nah am Team und am Code zu bleiben und Führung direkt und persönlich zu leben

  • Du bleibst hands-on bei Architekturentscheidungen und komplexen technischen Problemen und schaffst direkten Produkt-Impact
  • Du führst Dein Team als Doppelspitze mit der Produktmanagerin und arbeitest eng mit Senior Software Architekt und Head of Development zusammen

description: Deine Aufgaben Zahlen sind deine Leidenschaft, und du willst die Datenbasis dahinter nicht nur nutzen, sondern selbst gestalten? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig. Als Head of Finance & Data (m/w/d) bist du das strategische und technische Fundament für unser weiteres Wachstum. In dieser vielseitigen Doppelrolle verbindest du messerscharfe Zahlenkompetenz mit einem echten Gespür für Datenarchitektur und Reporting-Infrastruktur. Du baust nicht nur ein stabiles Controlling auf, sondern gestaltest parallel die technische Grundlage, auf der unser gesamtes Unternehmen datenbasierte Entscheidungen trifft. Kurz: Du hältst uns den Rücken frei und lenkst aktiv unseren Erfolgskurs mit. Strukturen schaffen: Du baust belastbare Controlling-Strukturen und Reportings mit einer klaren, zukunftsorientierten Steuerungslogik auf. Finanzen im Griff: Du übernimmst die Gesamtverantwortung für unsere Finanzplanung, das Reporting und die strategische finanzielle Steuerung. Data-Infrastruktur gestalten: Du treibst den Aufbau unserer automatisierten Datenpipelines voran (u. a. BigQuery, angebunden an Shopify, Klaviyo und weitere Quellen) und sorgst dafür, dass Kennzahlen zuverlässig, aktuell und zentral verfügbar sind. BI & Controlling verzahnen: Du entwickelst unsere Dashboards und Reporting-Tools (z. B. Looker Studio) so weiter, dass Finance-Kennzahlen und operative Daten in einem konsistenten Bild zusammenlaufen. Prozesse skalieren: Du etablierst effiziente, smarte Prozesse im Finance- und Data-Bereich, die mit uns mitwachsen. Sparring auf Augenhöhe: Du arbeitest eng mit unserem CEO zusammen und berätst ihn als geschätzter Sparringspartnerin in allen strategischen Finanz- und Datenfragen. Das steckt in deiner Haut Vorab: Niemand ist perfekt! Wenn du nicht jeden einzelnen Punkt zu 100 % erfüllst, uns aber mit deiner Motivation überzeugt, wollen wir dich trotzdem kennenlernen. Dein Fundament: Du blickst auf mehrjährige fundierte Erfahrung im Finance-Bereich zurück und bringst einen starken Background im Controlling mit. Du möchtest die Gesellschaft von morgen mitgestalten? Dann bist du bei ]init[ richtig. Denn unsere digitalen Lösungen sind für Menschen gemacht und haben gesellschaftliche Relevanz. Klingt spannend? Dann steig ein und arbeite gemeinsam mit über 1.200 ]init[s in interdisziplinären Teams an unseren sieben Standorten – oder flexibel von überall in Deutschland aus.


Deine Mission bei ]init[

Als Senior Frontend Angular Developer (all genders) realisierst du responsive und barrierefreie Oberflächen in strukturiertem, standardkonformem HTML5, CSS3 (SCSS), JavaScript und TypeScript. In Zusammenarbeit mit UXlern, Designer:innen, Kolleg:innen aus dem Development sowie Projektleiter:innen, verantwortest du die Erstellung der Frontends für verschiedene Kund:innen aus dem Public- und Private-Sector. Wenn du gern eigene Ideen einbringst und dich für eine abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit abseits starrer Denkmuster interessierst, würden wir uns freuen von dir zu hören.


Das gibt es zu tun

  • Du bist Teil eines interdisziplinären Teams und entwickelst Frontends auf Basis von Frameworks Angular und React.
  • In agilen Projekten arbeitest du eng mit den Kolleg:innen aus dem Backend, der Projektleitung und unseren Kund:innen zusammen.
  • Du unterstützt bei der Anforderungsanalyse, verfasst Spezifikationen und prüfst Lösungen hinsichtlich ihrer technischen Umsetzbarkeit.
  • Mit deinem Input sorgst du für die Weiterentwicklung bestehender Architekturen.
  • Du stehst sowohl unseren Kund:innen als auch deinen Kolleg:innen beratend zur Seite und analysierst sowie optimierst bestehende Prozesse.


Das bringst du mit

  • Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informatik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
  • Du begeisterst dich für kreative Lösungen und hast Spaß am Coden im agilen Umfeld.
  • Du kannst mehrjährige Kenntnisse in TypeScript, JavaScipt, HTML5 und CSS3 (SCSS), ES6 vorweisen.
  • Du verstehst zentrale Angular-Konzepte, setzt sie sicher ein und kannst mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung mit Angular und dem Angular-Ökosystem vorweisen.
  • Du hast erste Erfahrungen mit dem Framework React, was dich flexibel einsetzbar macht.
  • Clean Code ist kein Fremdwort für dich.
  • Du verfügst über angewandte Kenntnisse mit Atomic Design und BEM.
  • Wünschenswert sind Praxiserfahrungen in der Anforderungsanalyse und der Erstellung entsprechender Spezifikationen.
  • Du bist Teamplayer und hast Lust auf einen engen Austausch mit diversen Stakeholdern.
  • Du bringst sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift mit.


Das bieten wir dir

  • Because we care: 30 Urlaubstage und Workation innerhalb der EU schaffen Freiraum für Erholung und neue Perspektiven. So lassen sich Beruf und Privatleben gut miteinander verbinden.
  • Work with us: Flexible Arbeitszeiten, mobiles Arbeiten und Teilzeitmodelle ermöglichen dir, Arbeit und Alltag passend zu gestalten - immer abgestimmt mit deinem Team und deinen Projekten.
  • Learn with us: Mit der ]init[ Academy, Trainings, Zertifizierungen und bereichsübergreifendem Wissensaustausch entwickelst du dich fachlich und persönlich kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Grow with us: Profitiere von bereichsübergreifendem Wissensaustausch und entwickle dich gemeinsam mit deinen Kolleg:innen kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Ride with us: JobRad, ÖPNV-Zuschuss und weitere Mobility Benefits unterstützen dich dabei, flexibel und nachhaltig unterwegs zu sein.
  • Start with us: Welcome Week, strukturiertes Onboarding und Patenschaften sorgen für einen gelungenen Einstieg und helfen dir, schnell im Team und deinen Projekten anzukommen.


Werde Teil des Teams

Gestalte mit uns die digitale Zukunft - in Vollzeit oder Teilzeit, remote oder im Office.
Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung unter Angabe deines frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermins und deiner Gehaltsvorstellung.
Vielfalt und Chancengleichheit sind für uns selbstverständlich. Bewerbungen von Menschen mit Behinderung und Gleichstellung begrüßen wir ausdrücklich.

Da uns und unseren Kund:innen Sicherheit wichtig ist, kann je nach Position nach einer Zusage eine vertrauliche Sicherheitsüberprüfung erforderlich sein.


Recruiter

Marina Makridina

title: Working Student IT Strategy & Governance (all genders)
description: Über tonies: tonies ist die weltweit führende interaktive Audio-Plattform für Kinder mit mehr als 10 Millionen verkauften Tonieboxen und 125 Millionen verkauften Tonies. Das intuitive und preisgekrönte Audiosystem hat mit seinem kindersicheren, kabellosen und bildschirmfreien Ansatz die Art und Weise verändert, wie kleine Kinder selbstständig spielen und lernen. Tonieboxen wurden bereits in über 100 Ländern aktiviert und das Inhaltsportfolio umfasst rund 1.400 Tonies in mehreren Sprachen. Seit der Gründung hat tonies bedeutende Meilensteine erreicht – darunter den Börsengang an der Frankfurter Wertpapierbörse im November 2021 sowie ein weltweit präsentes Team von über 550 engagierten Experten, die aus verschiedenen Ländern agieren. Teil unseres tonies-Teams zu werden bedeutet, Teil einer inspirierenden Mission zu sein: innovative und bedeutungsvolle Erlebnisse für Kinder auf der ganzen Welt zu schaffen. Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Zukunft des Spielens, Lernens und der Fantasie. Du als Teil von tonies: Wir suchen einen motivierten Werkstudenten zur Verstärkung unseres IT Strategy & Governance Teams, der unsere Experten innerhalb der CIO- & CPO-Einheiten dabei unterstützt, das nachhaltige Wachstum von tonies voranzutreiben. Du wirst eng mit dem Enterprise Architect, dem IT Governance Analysten und dem Manager Trust & Security zusammenarbeiten, um die IT-Strategie, Standards und Leitplanken zu definieren. So ermöglichst du es den tonies-Mitarbeitenden, unserer wachsenden globalen Kundenbasis effektiv sichere und stabile Produkte mit einem skalierbaren Fundament zu bieten. Diese Rolle ist ideal für jemanden, der organisiert, zuverlässig und lernbegierig ist sowie Interesse daran hat, eine Karriere im IT-Bereich in einem internationalen Umfeld aufzubauen. Deine Aufgaben umfassen: IT-Strategie & Architektur Bewerten der tonies-Systemlandschaft im Hinblick auf den strategischen Fit. Unterstützen strategischer IT-Projekte (z. B. Stammdatenmanagement, Lizenzgebühren/Royalties, E-Commerce). Pflegen der Enterprise-Architektur-Dokumentation in LeanIX. IT-Governance & Sicherheit Vorqualifizieren neuer Software-Anfragen und Beraten fachübergreifender Stakeholder (IT, Data/AI, Einkauf, Legal). Pflegen des tonies-Applikationsportfolios (System Ownership, CIA-Scoring, Kosten, Nutzung etc.). Optimieren von Verlängerungsprozessen durch Unterstützung bei der Erstellung und Aktualisierung des Softwarelizenz-Verlängerungsplans. Aufsetzen und iteratives Weiterentwickeln von IT-Security-Onlinetrainingsmodulen für Mitarbeitende. Unterstützen von ISO 27001-, ITIL- und allgemeinen Compliance-Initiativen. Was wir uns von dir wünschen: Studienstatus: Derzeit eingeschrieben in einem Bachelor- oder Masterstudiengang (z. B. Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informatik, Informationsmanagement oder einem verwandten Bereich). Bereichsinteresse: Starkes Interesse an IT-Architektur, Enterprise Security und Governance-Standards. Denkweise: Bewusster Umgang mit modernen Tools – nach dem Motto „Think First, AI Second“. Tech Stack: Vertrautheit mit den gängigen Produktivitäts-Suites (Google Workspace oder Microsoft 365). Arbeitsweise: Strukturiert, zuverlässig und detailorientiert mit der Bereitschaft, Verantwortung für übertragene Aufgaben zu übernehmen. Soft Skills: Starke Kommunikationsfähigkeiten und die Fähigkeit, sowohl eigenständig als auch im Team zu arbeiten. Sprachen: Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse sind erforderlich (Englisch ist ein Plus). Warum tonies? Zu unseren Grundsätzen gehört es, dass wir uns bei tonies ® für Inklusion und Vielfalt einsetzen. Wir feiern die unterschiedlichen Fähigkeiten, Herkünfte, Glaubensvorstellungen und geschlechtlichen Identitäten, die sich unter unserem Dach vereinen. Jedes Gesicht ist bei uns willkommen und wird in allen Entwicklungsphasen mit und von uns unterstützt. Wir freuen uns auf deine digitale Bewerbung! title: (Senior / Staff) IT Operations Specialist (m/f/d)
description: 1KOMMA5° At 1KOMMA5° , we pursue a clear vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free . To make this a reality, we are building the energy system of the future with Heartbeat AI. Want to be part of it? We bring together regional craftsmanship and scalable software: We don't think of solar, batteries, heat pumps, and e-mobility as isolated components, but control them as an intelligent, integrated overall system in our virtual power plant. Directly connected to the electricity market – in real time, fully automated. This way, energy is used when it is available from renewables and particularly cost-effective. By 2030, our goal is to transition 1.5 million households to renewable energies. Over 3,000 people are working towards this every day, at more than 80 locations worldwide, from Finland to Australia. Want to take responsibility and build solutions that truly matter? Apply now and help us shape the energy world of tomorrow. Learn more about our Product & Tech team! Your mission As the (Senior / Staff) IT Operations Specialist, you will be the assigned Tech counterpart for the holding/central employees at 1KOMMA5. This means that every 1KOMMA5 employee in the holding will know their Tech Business Partner by name, and have trust to include them in all technical discussions that improve their productivity. You are accountable for the holdings success. The average day of a (Senior / Staff) IT Operations Specialist The role is divided into 3 key value areas Tech Support on level 1, 2 and 3 tickets created by holding employees. The goal here is to be familiar with stakeholders for faster, more efficient turnaround. Tickets are not escalated, but are triaged and discussed to improve technical understanding and develop. You will also monitor queues for the other markets for urgent out of hours requests, and action them when necessary. Level 1 and 2 tickets may be delegated to working students in the team, with guidance and accountability. Tech Projects - This refers to projects imposed by Employee Technology Platform product strategy such as rollout of Chrome OS and tool consolidations for the holding. This also refers to inbound projects imposed by holding teams (e.g. tailor onboarding experience, setup n8n flows). Jedox is a global leader in Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) and a recognized Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader, helping organizations transform fragmented planning into connected, data-driven decision-making. Trusted by more than 2,500 customers worldwide, Jedox enables business planning, budgeting and forecasting for finance, sales, and broader enterprise departments with leading-edge technology to outperform digital transformation and provide tangible customer value. At the heart of the platform is JedoxAI - a multi-agent intelligence engine delivering explainable, AI-powered forecasting, natural-language insights and AIssisted™ planning - putting Jedox at the forefront of the shift to AI-driven performance management. Your Responsibilities As a Sales Account Executive (m/f/d) within the Jedox team, you will play a key part in helping enterprise customers to transform their planning, forecasting and performance management processes. Acting as a trusted advisor, you will use a value-based sales approach to show how Jedox provides modern, digital and integrated enterprise performance and analysis (xP&A) solutions. In this role, you will own the entire sales process for enterprise customers, from identifying potential clients to closing deals. You will promote Jedox as the ideal solution for xP&A initiatives, work closely with internal teams and develop long-term relationships with customers and partners, while maintaining a strong focus on value, trust and sustainable success. We are building a high-performing team defined by ownership, accountability and energy. This is a genuinely exciting time to join: AI is reshaping how every finance team plans and forecasts, and Jedox is right at the centre of that conversation - giving you a fresh, differentiated story to take to market. If you're a motivated seller who enjoys being out in front of customers and partners, and want to make your mark in an exciting company, you'll find real support, momentum and opportunity here. You will own your number, your territory and your pipeline - creating opportunity rather than waiting for it, with a team around you that celebrates the wins together. Own the end-to-end sales cycle: Generate revenue by adopting a value-selling approach throughout the process, from initial engagement to closing enterprise-level deals - with full personal accountability for every outcome in your territory. Create and own high-quality pipeline: Build and maintain healthy pipeline coverage against your quota through proactive, self-generated prospecting - not just inbound - with disciplined weekly pipeline management in our CRM as the single source of truth. Communicate the value of Jedox: Demonstrate how Jedox and JedoxAI empower xP&A projects and elevate planning, forecasting and business decisions - bringing AI-driven, explainable forecasting into the conversation and anchoring every discussion on business outcomes, not features. Inspire digital transformation: Engage prospects by presenting a clear and compelling vision of digitisation and integrated business planning. Develop strategic sales plans: Identify, prospect and execute targeted sales plays and activities to win enterprise customers, including structured account planning, rigorous qualification (e.g. MEDDPICC) and multi-threading across finance, IT and operations stakeholders. Cross-functional collaboration: Acquire new customers by working closely with the pre-sales, channel management, marketing and business development teams - bringing colleagues and partners in early, and lifting each other up as one team with one number. Drive market-facing activity: Contribute to workshops, webinars and events alongside marketing and partners to create demand and build visible expertise in your market. Work smarter with AI: Actively use modern AI tools in your daily workflow - from account research and prospecting to preparing presentations, proposals and follow-ups - so more of your time goes where it counts: in front of customers and partners. Own forecasting and pipeline management: Maintain accurate monthly and quarterly forecasts as well as pipeline reports, with strong CRM hygiene, and play an active role in prospecting activities. Build lasting relationships: Build trusted partnerships with customers, partners and internal stakeholders to ensure long-term success. Your Profile Over three years' experience in professional sales, ideally within the FP&A function. Experience in Enterprise Performance Management or in selling analytics, AI, data, or ERP solutions. Strong record of success in achieving and exceeding sales goals. Proven ability to build, manage and self-generate a healthy sales pipeline and expand existing accounts. A high-ownership mindset: you act with urgency, take responsibility for your results, and when challenges arise you come with ideas on how to tackle them together. Resilience and positivity: you're the kind of person who stays positive, keeps going and enjoys the journey as much as the win. A love of being active in the market: you genuinely enjoy talking to customers and partners - on calls, in meetings and at events - and you know that's where great pipeline comes from. Strong collaboration skills with a clear focus on customer success and innovation. Confident, hands-on use of AI tools (such as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or similar) in your day-to-day selling - for example researching accounts, building presentations and business cases, sharpening messaging and working smarter across the sales cycle. Native or fluent English skills; an established network and knowledge of the UK & Ireland enterprise market are a real advantage. Transparency Note: Use of Artificial Intelligence As a tech-driven company, Jedox uses modern technologies — including AI — to continuously improve our processes. In recruiting, AI may support us in screening and structuring applications. It does not replace human judgment, but helps us reduce bias and ensure a consistent candidate experience. Your application is always reviewed by real people. If you would like to learn more about the process, please visit the website of our partner Hi People . raw.title: Office Assistant (Part Time) - UK
raw.description:
As the Office Assistant for Marqeta's London branch, your role will be pivotal in managing the office's requirements. You will be a proactive professional, trusted and respected for handling sensitive information and crucial relationships.

This is a part time role and performed in the office (Tuesday + Thursday) from our London office. We’d love for you to join us!

The Impact You'll have

  • Order supplies and manage office stock within a budget - drinks, snacks, stationary and equipment as needed.

  • Ensure the office is tidy and presentable.

  • Coordinate meeting room bookings.

  • Collect deliveries.

  • Support organisation of a variety of events (team meetings, offsites, meals, parties, etc.) within a set budget.

  • Working with vendors to organise and coordinate office wellness initiatives - Tuesday lunches, office massages.

  • Promote events within our office building.

  • Liaise with the building team regarding any issues that might arise.

  • Provide general support to visitors and manage tracking.

  • Address employees queries regarding office management issues (e.g. stationery, hardware, travel arrangements).

  • Provide general office management support and handle various projects as they arise, even unexpectedly.

  • Manage swag orders and distribution.

  • Support the organisation of charity initiatives.

  • Distribute new hire kits and manage stock.

  • Send communications to the team regarding office updates, events, birthdays, training etc.

 

Who You Are

  • Self-motivation, excellent organisation, strong work ethic and a proactive approach.

  • Flexibility and comfort in a fast-paced, high-intensity, yet informal startup environment.

  • Proven experience as an Office Manager, Front Office Manager or Administrative Assistant.

  • Knowledge of office administrator responsibilities, systems, and procedures.

  • Experience with office management software like MS Office and Google Suite.

  • Excellent time management skills and ability to multi-task and prioritize work.

  • Attention to detail and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong organisational and planning skills in a fast-paced environment.

  • A creative mind with an ability to suggest improvements.

  • Fluency in English.

     

Your Recruiter

  • Lou Devlin - Linkedin Profile (no agencies please!)

     

Typical Process

  • Application Submission

  • Recruiter video call

  • Hiring manager video call

  • Virtual “Onsite” consisting of 3 x 30 min calls

  • Offer!

     

Compensation and Benefits (for Full Time Roles)

  • Premium Private Medical and Dental coverage

  • Generous time off program with additional “Floating Holiday days”

  • Retirement savings program with company contribution

  • Equity in a publicly-traded company and an Employee Stock Purchase Program

  • Monthly stipend to support our remote work model

  • Annual development stipend to support our people's growth and development

  • Family-forming benefits and up to 20 weeks of Parental Leave

  • Wellbeing programs i.e. Modern Health, HealthKick and much more…

About Marqeta

Marqeta is on a mission to change the way money moves. We’re one of the earliest enablers of embedded finance, a market opportunity sized up in the trillions. Our card issuing platform provides unprecedented flexibility and control for companies to issue cards, authorize transactions, and manage payment operations in real time. Marqeta is powering the most well known brands in the new economy (Block, Cash App, Affirm, Instacart, Doordash, Uber, Walmart, etc). You don’t need to be a Payments expert to join the Marqeta Team, let us help you with that. This is the opportunity of a lifetime to work with innovators around the world and unlock equitable financial access for all.

Marqeta’s Values

– Solve for the Customer: With a deep understanding of our customers' business and empathy for their needs, we deliver products and services that drive their success. Earning and keeping their trust guides everything we do.

– Do What's Right: Knowing businesses and livelihoods depend on us, we pursue solutions that disrupt responsibly and deliver high-quality results that our customers count on. We own our work from start to finish.

– Simplify and Innovate: We approach challenges with curiosity and take smart risks. Innovation comes from finding better, simpler ways to achieve extraordinary outcomes.

– Win as a Team: We succeed together by embracing diverse perspectives and pushing each other to raise the bar. We lead with humility and set aside hierarchy to work as a team.

– Make it Count: We drive forward with focus and agility. With a sense of urgency and purpose, we get the job done, and done right.

Equal Employment Opportunity, Accommodations and Privacy

Marqeta is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, childbirth, or related medical conditions), veteran status or uniformed service member status, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship or immigration status, physical or mental disability, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information (including testing or characteristics) or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Marqeta endeavors to make reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to submit this application, complete any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participate in the employee selection process, please submit this form with your specific accommodation request.

Marqeta cares about your privacy. Personal data that is provided as part of the application and recruitment process is processed in accordance with the Applicant Privacy Notice. Additional information for California residents can be found here.

novel vulnerability types with the security community.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>10+ years of experience in security research, penetration testing, or offensive Rust.&nbsp;</li> <li>Ability to read and analyze code across multiple languages and codebases</li> <li>Strong knowledge of AI frameworks</li> <li>Strong understanding of AI attack vectors including recommendations</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with creative thinking about attack scenarios</li> <li><strong>Nice to Have: </strong>Published security research or conference title: Bookkeeper
description: Bookkeeper — Lab54 Location: London. All 3 days in office for the first three months. From month 4, 1 day per week remote once the agreed targets are being met. Shape: Part-time, 3 days per week. Permanent or contract — both considered. Salary: £30–34k FTE equivalent, pro-rata (£18–20.5k at 3 days). Contract equivalent £150–200 per day. Reports to: Financial Controller (interim: Managing Director) Start: As soon as available About Lab54 Lab54 is a content-led events and production company: [Anywhere But A Club.] We create high-impact experiences in unexpected locations, capture them, and turn them into content. Combined global audience of 425,000+. We work with brands, record labels and artists — around 100 events a year across brand activations, artist pop-ups, hard-ticket shows, house parties and festival takeovers. The role The Bookkeeper is Lab54's day-to-day finance function: reconciliation, purchase-order matching, receipt capture, invoicing, debtor chasing and payroll preparation. The defining feature of the job is that every pound has to land against an event. Lab54's core financial object isn't the month — it's the project. Each event carries a code (YYMM-Owner-Event-City) that runs from HubSpot through Xero, Teamwork and the purchase-order flow. Coding transactions to that project is not admin; it's the thing that makes per-event profitability computable. It is the single most important part of this role. This role prepares, never approves. All payment runs are approved by the Managing Director, with the CEO approving above an agreed threshold. Responsibilities Purchase orders and supplier ledger Match supplier invoices to their purchase order in Xero. This is a manual link, and it is the control that stops us paying more than we agreed. Enforce the PO rule at the front door: any commitment of £500 or more needs a PO, and an invoice arriving without a PO number goes back to the supplier rather than into the ledger. Prepare payment runs for approval. Nothing leaves the business without a bill, a PO and a sign-off. Reconcile supplier statements monthly against our purchase ledger — the check that catches duplicate invoices and payments before they're made. Maintain the purchase ledger and keep the aged creditor position accurate. Reconciliation and coding Bank and card reconciliations kept current within 48 hours, including Revolut Business card spend against Xero tracking categories. Every reconciled line matched to a real source document. A line that reconciles without a bill behind it is an exception to raise, not a box to tick. Code every transaction to the correct project code and tracking category. Chase the team when a code is missing rather than guessing one. Keep the suspense and uncoded accounts at nil by month-end. Produce a weekly untagged-spend report, by spender, and drive it to zero. Receipts and VAT recovery Chase and capture missing receipts to a 98% target. This is a cash exercise, not a filing one — every missing VAT invoice is input VAT we can't reclaim. Flag transactions carrying no VAT treatment where the supplier is UK VAT-registered. Prepare the VAT return workings for the external accountancy firm, who own submission. Sales invoicing and debtors Raise client invoices within 48 hours of the billing trigger, coded to the project. Own debtor chasing end to end — a consistent cycle, escalated when it stalls, so nobody else in the business is carrying it. Match incoming receipts to the right invoice and contact. Money that arrives against the wrong customer looks identical to money that never arrived. Keep sales invoice sequencing clean — anything voided or reissued carries a recorded reason. Project close When a project closes, produce its final position: budgeted cost against actual cost, budgeted revenue against invoiced revenue, and the resulting margin. Issue that to the CEO and Operations Director as a matter of routine. It is not a report anyone should have to request. Late costs land after an event has finished — that's the nature of the business. The job is to make sure they land against the right project and that the closing number reflects them. Cash and reporting Produce a weekly cash one-pager: bank position, overdue debtors with days outstanding, payment runs due, projected balance. Keep the company's master P&L model current — updating actuals and committed costs as they change, so the forecast reflects where the business genuinely is. raw.title: Bookkeeper
raw.description:
Bookkeeper — Lab54

Location: London. All 3 days in office for the first three months. From month 4, 1 day per week remote once the agreed targets are being met.

Shape: Part-time, 3 days per week. Permanent or contract — both considered.

Salary: £30–34k FTE equivalent, pro-rata (£18–20.5k at 3 days). Contract equivalent £150–200 per day.

Reports to: Financial Controller (interim: Managing Director)

Start: As soon as available

About Lab54

Lab54 is a content-led events and production company: [Anywhere But A Club.]

We create high-impact experiences in unexpected locations, capture them, and turn them into content. Combined global audience of 425,000+. We work with brands, record labels and artists — around 100 events a year across brand activations, artist pop-ups, hard-ticket shows, house parties and festival takeovers.

The role

The Bookkeeper is Lab54's day-to-day finance function: reconciliation, purchase-order matching, receipt capture, invoicing, debtor chasing and payroll preparation.

The defining feature of the job is that every pound has to land against an event. Lab54's core financial object isn't the month — it's the project. Each event carries a code (YYMM-Owner-Event-City) that runs from HubSpot through Xero, Teamwork and the purchase-order flow. Coding transactions to that project is not admin; it's the thing that makes per-event profitability computable. It is the single most important part of this role.

This role prepares, never approves. All payment runs are approved by the Managing Director, with the CEO approving above an agreed threshold.

Responsibilities

Purchase orders and supplier ledger

  • Match supplier invoices to their purchase order in Xero. This is a manual link, and it is the control that stops us paying more than we agreed.
  • Enforce the PO rule at the front door: any commitment of £500 or more needs a PO, and an invoice arriving without a PO number goes back to the supplier rather than into the ledger.
  • Prepare payment runs for approval. Nothing leaves the business without a bill, a PO and a sign-off.
  • Reconcile supplier statements monthly against our purchase ledger — the check that catches duplicate invoices and payments before they're made.
  • Maintain the purchase ledger and keep the aged creditor position accurate.

Reconciliation and coding

  • Bank and card reconciliations kept current within 48 hours, including Revolut Business card spend against Xero tracking categories.
  • Every reconciled line matched to a real source document. A line that reconciles without a bill behind it is an exception to raise, not a box to tick.
  • Code every transaction to the correct project code and tracking category. Chase the team when a code is missing rather than guessing one.
  • Keep the suspense and uncoded accounts at nil by month-end.
  • Produce a weekly untagged-spend report, by spender, and drive it to zero.

Receipts and VAT recovery

  • Chase and capture missing receipts to a 98% target. This is a cash exercise, not a filing one — every missing VAT invoice is input VAT we can't reclaim.
  • Flag transactions carrying no VAT treatment where the supplier is UK VAT-registered.
  • Prepare the VAT return workings for the external accountancy firm, who own submission.

Sales invoicing and debtors

  • Raise client invoices within 48 hours of the billing trigger, coded to the project.
  • Own debtor chasing end to end — a consistent cycle, escalated when it stalls, so nobody else in the business is carrying it.
  • Match incoming receipts to the right invoice and contact. Money that arrives against the wrong customer looks identical to money that never arrived.
  • Keep sales invoice sequencing clean — anything voided or reissued carries a recorded reason.

Project close

  • When a project closes, produce its final position: budgeted cost against actual cost, budgeted revenue against invoiced revenue, and the resulting margin.
  • Issue that to the CEO and Operations Director as a matter of routine. It is not a report anyone should have to request.
  • Late costs land after an event has finished — that's the nature of the business. The job is to make sure they land against the right project and that the closing number reflects them.

Cash and reporting

  • Produce a weekly cash one-pager: bank position, overdue debtors with days outstanding, payment runs due, projected balance.
  • Keep the company's master P&L model current — updating actuals and committed costs as they change, so the forecast reflects where the business genuinely is.
  • The model is ours; you update the numbers within it. Structural or formula changes come to the CEO first.

Payroll preparation

  • Prepare payroll data and submit it to the external payroll provider ahead of deadline.
  • Post the payroll journal to Xero each month. Wages must not sit in a control account.
  • Confirm the payroll account is funded before each run. This role does not execute payroll.

Close, deadlines and records

  • Run the monthly close to a published working-day deadline: accruals prepared with supporting detail, journals posted, period locked.
  • Every accrual carries a schedule — supplier, event, date of work. No balance we can't explain.
  • Maintain the statutory deadline register (VAT, PAYE, corporation tax, Companies House) and flag each one in advance. No filing sits invisibly in someone else's workflow.
  • Keep records orderly and audit-ready for the external accountancy firm.

What the first 90 days actually look like

We are being straight about this because we want someone who finds it interesting rather than alarming.

Lab54 has grown faster than its finance function, and we've recently changed accountants. The ledger carries a real backlog: untagged transactions across two financial years, unposted payroll journals, a month-end close that has not been run to a cadence, and a purchase-order process that has only just gone live. There is a documented correction schedule and an external FD working through it.

The first 90 days is a clean-up, not a steady state.

Days 1–30. Learn the ledger and the project-code structure. Take over reconciliation, receipt capture and PO matching. Get the weekly untagged report running.

Days 31–60. Clear the untagged backlog. Take over sales invoicing, debtor chasing and received-payment matching. Payroll preparation and the monthly payroll journal move across.

Days 61–90. Run a full month close to deadline: suspense at nil, every accrual scheduled, supplier statements reconciled. Per-project cost data becomes reportable for the first time.

After that it becomes a genuinely well-defined job inside a documented control structure — and you'll have built it.

On being in the office. The first three months are fully office-based, and that's deliberate rather than a policy position. Clearing a backlog this size means asking people questions in real time — whose card that was, what the missing PO covers, which event a supplier belongs to. That's an hour of work in a room and a week of work over email. From month 4, one of the three days moves to remote, provided the measures below are being met.

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Proven bookkeeping experience. Xero to a high standard is non-negotiable — tracking categories, purchase orders, bank rules, manual journals.
  • Purchase-order matching and supplier statement reconciliation as routine practice.
  • A project- or job-costing background — agency, events, production, construction, consultancy, anywhere the job rather than the month is the unit of profit. This is the part of the role we can't train quickly.
  • Strong reconciliation, coding and purchase-ledger discipline.
  • Experience preparing payroll data for an external provider and posting the payroll journal.
  • Comfortable working inside a defined control structure where you prepare and someone else approves.
  • Reliability over ambition. The value of this role is that nothing is ever late or missing.

Nice to have

  • Multi-currency invoicing and foreign supplier payments. We run events across Europe.
  • Dext, Revolut Business, or similar capture and expense tooling.
  • Experience cleaning up a ledger rather than only maintaining a tidy one.

How you'll work

  • Meticulous. Proactive on receipts, POs and debtors — chasing people is part of the job, not an escalation.
  • Willing to say when something doesn't look right. A number you can't explain is a question, not a rounding difference.
  • Discreet and trustworthy with company finances.

Financial reporting and month-end close

  • Own the integrity of the UK&Europe balance sheet, with reconciliations that stay current, reviewed and explainable

  • Be the single point of contact for group finance on anything UK&Europe: queries, adjustments, restatements, consolidation-level questions

Compliance and risk oversight

  • Own the UK&Europe compliance calendar (Companies House, HMRC, VAT) by directing external accountants and advisers

  • Own the adviser relationships (accounting, tax, audit), keeping work well scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi's internal finance standards

  • Build an early-warning process so compliance risk is caught and escalated well before it threatens trading status

  • Be the accountable owner if something in the compliance chain breaks down

Commercial business partnering

  • Be the day-to-day finance partner to UK&Europe leadership, owning the regional P&L narrative, budget vs actual and the "why" behind the numbers

  • Bring a commercial lens to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, flagging risk and opportunity early

  • Translate regional performance into clear, decision-ready input for FP&A and company leadership

  • Give UK&Europe business leaders a reliable, self-serve view of their numbers, so decisions stop waiting on Australian hours

  • Feed central finance the regional inputs it needs at close: accrual estimates, revenue and spend context, then review and sign off on the UK&Europe result

  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success to resolve aged and disputed balances and unblock stuck revenue

  • Own the commercial view of collection risk: which accounts, why, and what it means for cash, and feed it into forecasting

  • Drive down UK&Europe DSO by fixing the upstream causes (contracting, disputes, process), not by chasing invoices

FinOps, controls and performance frameworks

  • Build the operating rhythm that turns UK&Europe finance from reactive support into a reliable performance framework: clear KPIs, owners, review cadences and escalation paths

  • Partner with budget owners on spend decisions before they are made, rather than policing them after the fact

  • Strengthen financial controls across spend, approvals, vendor onboarding, card usage, subscriptions and commercial commitments, while keeping the process pragmatic for a fast-moving region

  • Review regional AP and card activity, including prompt removal of leaver access and cards, and escalate anomalies to central finance operations

  • Partner with external accountants, tax advisers, compliance providers and other vendors, making sure work is well-scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi’s internal finance standards

  • Use FinOps-style discipline to connect spend, usage and outcomes, especially across tooling, GTM systems, implementation costs and region-specific operating expenses

  • Create simple documentation and control checks so the region can scale without relying on informal knowledge or one-off fixes

What you'll need

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen — comfortable moving between P&L narrative, deal economics and cash impact

  • Experience business partnering with Sales, Customer Success or regional leadership in a growth business

  • Track record improving collections or DSO by fixing root causes, not just process

  • Experience owning spend or expense controls in a way that supports the business rather than only governing it

  • Comfortable directing (not necessarily performing) statutory compliance and VAT work through external advisers

  • High degree of autonomy and ownership in a small, remote-first global finance team

  • Clear, confident communicator — able to hold your own with commercial leaders and external advisers alike

  • Experience in a multi-entity or multi-currency business

Nice to have

  • Experience in a high-growth SaaS or technology company

  • Qualified accountant (ACA / ACCA / CIMA or equivalent)

  • Exposure to Companies House, HMRC and Irish Revenue processes

  • Experience with Campfire, Airwallex or similar modern finance tooling

You'll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We're medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who've felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we're building isn't always easy. But we didn't choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn't whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you're doing the defining work of your career.

raw.title: Director of Go-to-Market Engineering
raw.description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including On Running, Breitling, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.


About the Role

We are hiring our first Director of Go-to-Market Engineering.

Perk's revenue organisation is 800 people selling to more than 10,000 companies. Behind them sits a CRM, an enrichment and signal stack, a growing set of AI agents - and a lot of manual work that no longer needs to exist. Your job is to remove it and to build the automated systems that replace it.

You will own GTM Engineering end-to-end: which tools we use, how the architecture fits together, what gets built, and what it does for revenue. You report to the VP of Revenue Operations, lead a small senior team across Europe and North America, and work across SDR, Account Executive, and Account Management - a few high-impact projects each quarter.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it. You will be in Clay, in the orchestration logic, in the agent workflows, building alongside a team doing the same. You're using your experience to guide and coach them to accelerate the pace.

The other half of the job is commercial. The best GTM engineers we have met can sit with a regional Sales VP, work out why their pipeline isn't converting, and leave with the right thing to build. That instinct matters more to us than any single tool on a CV.

What You'll Do

Own the strategy and the stack

  • Define Perk's GTM engineering architecture - how CRM, enrichment, signal, sequencing, orchestration and data layers fit together.

  • Make the tooling calls: what we adopt, what we consolidate, what we retire, and why it pays for itself.

  • Set the roadmap with the VP of Revenue Operations, Sales leadership, and the Revenue Systems and Data teams.

  • Establish the standards the team builds to - version control, documentation, testing, and rollback.

Build, hands-on

  • Design and build in Clay: tables, waterfall enrichment, AI columns, webhooks and API integrations in production.

  • Own the orchestration layer - the logic deciding which records enter a workflow, when, and on what criteria. This is where GTM automation succeeds or fails.

  • Build agentic workflows on modern LLM and agent tooling to take research, qualification, summarisation and data entry off people entirely.

  • Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

Automate across SDR, AE, and AM

  • Own account prospecting automation globally: TAM sourcing, enrichment, ICP and intent scoring, prioritisation and distribution.

  • Give AEs their selling time back - CRM autofill, quoting, meeting prep, opportunity hygiene, first outbounds.

  • Build account intelligence for Account Management: risk signals, whitespace, account planning.

  • Take each project from prototype to production properly - instrumented and validated before it scales.

Bridge commercial and technical

  • Turn commercial problems into technical architecture, and technical output into impact a revenue VPs recognises.

  • Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.

  • Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team

  • Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.

  • Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

  • Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

What Will Make You Successful

Experience

  • Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

  • Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team

  • Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft

  • Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.

  • Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.

  • Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.

  • Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.

  • Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. Nobody has all of it. We care that you have real depth somewhere and can learn the rest quickly.

Commercial instinct

  • You judge your work by whether it moved a commercial metric, not by whether it shipped.

  • You have the credibility with Sales leaders to scope the right build - and to say when automation is the wrong answer.

  • You understand the funnel end to end: TAM, ICP, pipeline generation, conversion, expansion, and the economics underneath.

Nice to have

  • Having stood up a GTM engineering function at a high-growth SaaS business, ideally above $100M ARR.

  • Experience taking an automation programme from pilot to global production, including what you learned when it got bumpy.

  • Multi-region GTM experience across EMEA and North America.

Why This Role

GTM Engineering is a discipline being written right now, and most companies are still treating it as a tooling function. This is the chance to own it properly, the stack, the architecture, the build, and the commercial outcome across a $300M+ revenue business with 800 people in the field, a genuine appetite for automation, and the budget and executive backing to move fast.

You would be the first person in this seat, with real systems and real data to work with rather than a blank page, and the freedom to decide what Perk's automation layer should look like. There is a lot to go after, the problems are interesting, and the impact is immediate and visible.

If you want to build the automation layer of a commercial engine at this scale and you want to still have your hands on it come and build it here.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. The CEO Office The CEO Office works with senior leaders across Checkout.com on high-priority strategic and operational problems. The team turns important questions into clear decisions, coordinated execution and measurable business outcomes. The role This is a manager-level individual-contributor role for a hands-on operator. You will own defined, high-priority, cross-functional initiatives end to end—from framing problems and aligning stakeholders to implementing solutions and delivering measurable outcomes. Working closely with the Head of the CEO Office, you will combine structured problem-solving with hands-on execution. You will translate priorities into coordinated action, strengthen how teams operate and drive initiatives through to impact. This is neither a traditional PMO nor a presentation-led strategy role, and it is not an executive-level position. Success requires sound judgement, analytical rigour, clear communication, operational follow-through and the ability to influence effectively without formal authority. How You'll Make an Impact (Role overview) Support the CEO and Head of the CEO Office on critical cross-functional initiatives by helping coordinate day-to-day delivery, stakeholder collaboration and progress towards measurable outcomes. Help investigate complex, ambiguous problems by clarifying the problem, developing practical solutions and supporting the implementation of durable processes or systems. Support departments in scaling by contributing to organisation design, objectives and KPI setting, and the development of robust operating processes. Assist leadership in navigating ambiguity by surfacing insights, decisions and risks, coordinating follow-through and supporting alignment across teams, particularly where there is no natural owner. Projects may include organisational model design, international expansion strategy, scaling new business lines, strategic planning and goal setting, go-to-market execution, regulatory, data and financial infrastructure initiatives, and supporting board and shareholder reporting. What We're Looking For (Background and core competencies) Relevant background and impact: Experience in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.Relevant backgrounds include consulting, high-growth technology, investing, investment banking, strategic finance or entrepreneurial operations. Influence and collaboration: Build trust, navigate trade-offs and make progress across functions without formal authority, with a low-ego and collaborative approach. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. The Enterprise Business team at Airwallex helps ambitious businesses operate globally by providing the financial infrastructure they need to manage payments, money movement and related financial operations. The Account Management team works strategically to maximise the enterprise customer-Airwallex partnership by building trust, identifying and driving new revenue streams, and ensuring operational success.. You will work alongside , Leadership, Solutions Engineering, Product, Operations,Legal, GTM Partnerships, Customer Success, Finance and Revenue Strategy & Operations. The team operates with a high level of ownership and collaboration, managing complex customer needs and contributing directly to enterprise growth.

What you’ll do

As an Account Manager on the Enterprise team, you will manage a portfolio of strategic enterprise customers and help them maximise Airwallex value. You will build trusted relationships across commercial, finance, operations, product and technology stakeholders, while identifying opportunities to increase adoption, retain customers and expand their use of Airwallex’s products and markets. You will combine strategic account planning with hands-on ownership of upsells, , escalations, onboarding and complex customer initiatives. Working cross-functionally, you will turn customer insights into action and contribute to the growth of Airwallex’s Enterprise Business. This role is a quota-carrying commercial role and is based in London, UK.

Responsibilities:

  • Grow gross profit from existing customer accounts, manage customer operational success, and pursue upsell and expansion opportunities across Airwallex’s product suite.

  • Build and execute strategic account plans, including customer objectives, stakeholder maps, risks, renewal plans and 12 to 18-month growth opportunities.

  • Lead renewals, commercial negotiations, upsell and cross-sell opportunities, using data and customer insight to improve retention and drive Net Revenue Retention.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior customer stakeholders and run effective business reviews that demonstrate value, address risks and align on future priorities.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records, opportunity tracking and forecasts, while sharing customer feedback that can inform product, operational and go-to-market improvements.

Who you are

We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.

  • A data-driven approach to account health, forecasting, renewal planning and commercial prioritisation, with strong CRM discipline.
